svg.text: VX_cta_dispatch — admission, expansion, context, retirement
One CTA is accepted per IDLE→DISPATCH transition and expanded into warps at one warp per cycle. Everything expensive is kept off the kmu_bus_if.ready path.
ADMISSION — the ready path
kmu_bus_if.slave
kmu_req = kmu_req_t'(kmu_bus_if.data)
fragment kind: grid (1,1,1), block_size = count×4 lanes, cluster 1
Per-kernel constants — computed ONCE, registered
stride = kmu_req.aligned_lmem_size
usable_slots_r = max m in [1,NUM_WARPS] : m*stride <= LMEM_SIZE
a NUM_WARPS-wide comparator tree — constant×variable, so no divider
Slot window selection
base_tail = (tail_r >= usable_slots_r) ? 0 : tail_r
cluster_k = clamp(eff_cluster_size, 1, usable_slots_r)
cluster_prewrap = is_first && (base_tail + cluster_k > usable)
base_slot = cluster_prewrap ? 0 : base_tail
pre-wrap keeps a cluster window contiguous rather than split across the wrap
admit_ok — one slot, or the whole window
cluster_window = ((1 << cluster_k) - 1) << base_slot
admit_ok = is_first ? ((slot_valid_r & cluster_window) == 0)
: ~slot_valid_r[base_slot]
kmu_bus_if.ready = (state == IDLE) && admit_ok
&& !rem_warps_write_r && !frag_inflight
EXPANSION — one warp per cycle
FSM — two states, and that is all
IDLE : kmu_bus_if_fire -> latch descriptor, claim base_slot,
tail_r <= next_tail, state <= DISPATCH
DISPATCH : emit one warp per cycle until is_last_warp
a CTA is admitted only from IDLE, so admission and expansion never overlap
Free-warp selection
VX_priority_encoder(~(active_warps | dispatched_warps))
dispatched_warps is cleared at accept, so a warp already handed to this
CTA is not offered twice before the scheduler marks it active.
Power-of-two NUM_THREADS arithmetic — zero adders
cta_num_warps = block_size[hi] + |block_size[lo] // ceil div
block_size_next = {block_size[hi] - 1, block_size[lo]}
is_full_warp = |block_size_cur[hi]
partial_tmask = (1 << block_size_cur[lo]) - 1
NUM_THREADS is a power of two, so every divide here is a bit slice.
to VX_scheduler — the launch handshake
cta_fire, cta_wid, cta_PC, cta_tmask, cta_param, cta_init
The scheduler sets active_warps[wid], warp_pcs[wid] and thread_masks[wid],
and latches mscratch_r[wid] from cta_param. Nothing else crosses.
CONTEXT — BRAM, not per-warp flops
The per-lane TID ripple pipeline
SimX derives a lane’s thread coordinate by DIVISION at CSR-read time. RTL cannot
afford a runtime divider, so it precomputes every lane at launch: lane 0 is the warp
base, each later lane is +1 in X with a single carry into Y then Z.
TID_STEP = 2 TID_STAGES = (NUM_THREADS - 1 + 1) / 2
Serial by nature, so pipelined 2 lanes/cycle. The write latency is free: cta_warp_ram is
read many cycles later (fetch/decode/issue ≫ TID_STAGES).
cta_warp_ram
SIZE NUM_WARPS
RDW_MODE "R", OUT_REG 1
per warp:
cta_rank
lane_launch[NUM_THREADS]
cta_ctx_ram
SIZE NUM_CTA_MAX
RDW_MODE "R", OUT_REG 1
per CTA slot:
cta_size, block_idx, block_dim,
grid_dim, param, lmem_addr, ...
lane_launch is an OVERLAY, not a concatenation
A warp is launched EITHER as a compute warp (the lane carries its expanded {x,y,z} thread
index, read as CTA_THREAD_ID_*) OR as a fragment warp (the lane carries one slice of its
quad’s stamp, read as FRAG_*). They are alternatives: a raster-pushed fragment warp has no
block_dim, so a thread index is not merely unused but undefined — exactly as a real GPU’s
fragment shader has gl_FragCoord and no threadIdx. So they are ONE resource.
The RAM is only NUM_WARPS deep — entirely width-bound in BRAM, so the lane width is what costs area.
RETIREMENT — free the slot, out of order
T0 — the event
warp_done = tmc_valid
&& (tmc.tmask == 0)
done_slot = cta_slot_per_warp_r[wid]
a flop array: combinational read
T1 — the read
warp_done_r, done_slot_r latched
rem_warps_ram.read issued
retirement exclusively owns the
read port — no contention
T2 — the decision
cta_done = (rdata_fwd == 1)
slot_valid_r[slot] <= 0
the slot — and the LMEM region
at slot×stride — frees at once
Why two shadow registers and not one
Back-to-back retirements to the same slot would read a stale count, so the read result is forwarded from the pending write. It takes TWO stages because
the RAM is RDW_MODE="R" with OUT_REG=1: a read sampled in the same cycle as a write returns the PRE-write value, so the write stays invisible for two cycles.
rem_warps_rdata_fwd = (write_r && waddr_r == done_slot_r_dly) ? wdata_r // 1-cycle gap: write set last cycle
: (write_rr && waddr_rr == done_slot_r_dly) ? wdata_rr // 2-cycle gap: write not yet visible
: rem_warps_rdata;
Switching the RAM to RDW_MODE="W" would collapse the _rr shadow and the second compare — the one open item in this block.
COMPLETION
BUSY MUST COVER THE ACCEPT CYCLE
busy = (state == DISPATCH) || kmu_bus_if_fire
The accept→DISPATCH transition is registered, so gating on `state` alone leaves the
accept cycle un-busy. At SOCKET_SIZE>1 the socket busy aggregation is itself registered,
so on the final CTA kmu_busy drops before the buffered per-core busy rises — a 1-cycle
device-idle gap the host’s edge-sensitive wait latches as premature completion.
cta_init — the per-lane startup record
The startup stub derives each lane’s stack from its hart id, so a warp slot relaunched
with lanes it has not run before must run the stub again — this is tracked per LANE,
not per warp. A new ctx_id clears the whole record.
warp_pcs_n[wid] = cta_init ? cta_PC : (warp_pcs[wid] - 20)
reusing a warp rewinds to a fixed 5-instruction per-CTA dispatch window instead
The organising principle: the admission handshake is a critical path, so nothing expensive is allowed on it
What was moved OFF the ready path
• the occupancy bound — registered into usable_slots_r,
so admission sees a free-slot test, never a divide/encode
• the LMEM base multiply — latched at accept into
cur_lmem_base_r, not resolved during the handshake
• the warp count — captured at accept into cta_size_r,
so retirement keeps the RAM read port to itself
What is left: a mask compare against slot_valid_r.
Why a fixed stride and not a byte ring
The predecessor packed variable-size CTAs into a byte-level
ring — head/tail/free_size, wrap padding, in-order reclaim.
But the KMU runs ONE kernel at a time, so every resident CTA
has the SAME aligned_lmem_size. Packing N equal blocks into
a ring yields exactly floor(LMEM/stride) of them — identical
to a fixed partition, with zero wrap waste and no carry chain
on the handshake. The ring’s one advantage — dense packing of
mixed sizes — is never exercised.
Out-of-order slot reuse is safe — by construction
A freed slot always reuses its OWN LMEM region, because slot i’s
base is pinned at i×stride for the whole kernel. Nothing moves.
And cluster contiguity does not depend on reclaim order either:
it is established by the consecutive-slot reservation taken at
ADMIT. The byte ring’s in-head-order reclaim constraint — the
thing that forced retirement to be a serialised walk — is gone.
This is what NVIDIA/AMD do: occupancy is computed once at launch.
